'''Blackburn Rovers Football Club''' is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Blackburn]], Lancashire, England, which competes in the {{English football updater|BlackbuR}}, the second level of the [[English football league system]]. They have played home matches at [[Ewood Park]] since 1890. The club's motto is {{lang|la|Arte et Labore}}, meaning "By Skill and Hard Work" in Latin. They have a long-standing rivalry with nearby club [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], with whom they contest the [[East Lancashire derby]].

Blackburn Rovers was founded in 1875, becoming a founding member of [[English Football League|The Football League]] in 1888. They won five [[FA Cup]] finals in the 19th century: [[1884 FA Cup Final|1884]], [[1885 FA Cup Final|1885]], [[1886 FA Cup Final|1886]], [[1890 FA Cup Final|1890]] and [[1891 FA Cup Final|1891]]. The team was crowned [[List of English football champions|English League champions]] in 1911–12 and 1913–14, then won a sixth FA Cup in [[1928 FA Cup Final|1928]]. They were relegated for the first time in 1936, but returned to the top-flight as [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] champions in 1938–39. Relegated in 1948, Rovers secured promotion again in 1957–58, but were relegated in 1966 and again in 1971. Blackburn won the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] title in 1974–75, and were again promoted in 1979–80 after suffering relegation the previous year. They won the [[Full Members' Cup]] in [[1987 Full Members' Cup Final|1987]].

In 1992, Rovers gained promotion to the new [[Premier League]] via the [[1992 Football League Second Division play-off Final|play-offs]], a year after being taken over by local entrepreneur [[Jack Walker]], who installed [[Kenny Dalglish]] as manager. In [[1994–95 FA Premier League|1994–95]], Rovers became Premier League champions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/when-saturday-comes-blog/2013/oct/23/blackburn-premier-league-title-earned-1995 |title=Blackburn didn't buy the Premier League title in 1995 – they earned it |first=Jimmy |last=Pierce |date=23 October 2013 |work=The Guardian |access-date=15 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616061928/https://www.theguardian.com/football/when-saturday-comes-blog/2013/oct/23/blackburn-premier-league-title-earned-1995 |archive-date=16 June 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> Relegated four seasons after being crowned champions, they secured promotion in 2001, and won the [[2002 Football League Cup Final|Football League Cup Final]] the following year. They spent eleven successive seasons in the Premier League, but were relegated in 2012 and again into the third tier in 2017. Blackburn secured promotion out of [[2017–18 EFL League One|League One]] at the end of the 2017–18 season."}}
